topic:
Sharp generic single-edge identification degree beyond trees, with fasttreeid as the software consumer (exactid; field target). Let G=(V,D,B) be a known acyclic mixed graph on n>=2 vertices, bows allowed, containing a supplied rooted spanning arborescence T and at most k additional directed edges, where 0<=k<=(n-1)(n-2)/2. The Gaussian linear SCM has arbitrary real directed coefficients and positive-definite noise covariance Omega with zeros at missing bidirected pairs; its exact observed covariance is Sigma=(I-Lambda)^(-T)Omega(I-Lambda)^(-1). In the complexified source function field L=C(lambda_D,omega_B,omega_diag), let K_G=C(sigma_ij) be the covariance subfield. Define d_e(G)=[K_G(lambda_e):K_G] when algebraic, infinity otherwise, and D_k(n)=max finite d_e(G) over this entire graph class and directed-edge queries. This is SINGLE-COORDINATE complex generic degree, not whole-fiber degree, real root count, or local Jacobian rank.

KERNEL: determine D_k(n) sharply for EVERY admissible (n,k), by an explicit formula or structural recurrence solely in n,k, a universal upper bound and constructive attaining graph families. Give a complete randomized algorithm on (G,T,e,delta) returning d_e and, when finite, its monic minimal polynomial over K_G with coefficients represented by rational arithmetic circuits in covariance entries. Supply an explicit proper algebraic exceptional set outside which the polynomial's roots are exactly the complex queried-coordinate projection. Require construction time and certificate length n^{C(k+1)} poly(log(1/delta)) for universal C in a specified exact-arithmetic/PIT model, with symbolic error probability at most delta. The exact frontier, recurrence and mechanics remain answer-open; the sharpness, full size scope and certificate guarantees are commitments. Generic exposure plus black-box elimination alone is not the hard theorem. For regular positive-definite specializations separately retain real roots iff they extend to real directed coefficients satisfying the missing-bidirected equations; positive definiteness of recovered Omega follows by congruence. Do not assert real uniqueness from complex degree or local rank.

ESTIMATION RUNG: at fixed G,n and compact smooth covariance-model subsets with certificate denominators bounded away from zero, simple uniformly separated retained roots, and locally constant real-extension status, construct a sample-covariance/model-projection finite-set estimator with root-m sample-size Hausdorff rate and simultaneous asymptotic branch confidence neighborhoods. On singleton real fibers derive consistency and asymptotic normality. No discriminant-uniform inference or unjustified branch selection is claimed.

Grounding: Gupta-Blaser AAAI2024 arXiv2311.14058 Theorem27 and Lemmas4/12/25 give scalar Mobius tree identification; Briefs-Blaser NeurIPS2025 accelerates the same 1/2/infinite tree predicate. Hollering-Misra-Sturma arXiv2604.20516 Theorems4.4/5.1 concern bounded-degree RATIONAL FORMULAS, not algebraic fiber degree. Foygel-Draisma-Drton arXiv1107.5552 already has higher-degree small SEMs, so one cubic/quartic example is not novel. The named consumer https://cran.r-universe.dev/fasttreeid/doc/manual.html currently accepts one parent per node and returns 0/1/2 with path/fraction/cycle certificates; this theorem extends that same workflow to added parents and higher finite ambiguity. INTERNAL ANTI-CONSTRAINT: active/eid_fanin_numedge_frontier's numerical bounded-two-parent supplied-covariance predicate and residual handle are occupied. Do not relabel that numerical algorithm, omit the sharp generic frontier, or claim its all-singular-covariance scope. A six-node tree-plus-one-arrow legal SPD witness has four distinct real pole-free values of one coefficient, recovered from two conics; exact verification files accompany the draft.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The draft derives a proposed 2^(k+1) single-coordinate upper bound by freezing a coordinate transcendence basis, selecting residual Jacobian equations, and counting prescribed-indegree orientations in multihomogeneous Bezout. A one-sink family on 2k+4 vertices makes one original coefficient separate every branch. Exact rational checks verify degree-eight and degree-sixteen examples with positive-definite covariances and real simple branches; 715 bounded orientation graphs passed. Source-integral rank-one anchoring and Mobius propagation yield a proposed quadratic core in at most 2k coefficients. Positive-dimensional localization, zero/zero interactions, poles, real-extension limitations, and joint-versus-coordinate degree were checked. Old cubic/quartic examples and the active numerical handle are not novelty claims.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the size-sensitive orientation-realization theorem, correcting forced covariance relations or infinity roots, to determine D_k(n) and attain it for every smaller n. The full symbolic complexity, exceptional-set certificate and regular real-set inference still require the draft's listed proofs; do not substitute the established-looking large-n result for the original all-n kernel.
EARLY KILL TEST: Resolve rooted five-node k<=2 orientation predictions by exact saturated coordinate elimination, first lifting the modular quartic to characteristic zero. A strict gap stops the uncorrected realization conjecture; absent a tractable correction, pivot the all-n scope.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_extra_parent_degree.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp size-sensitive maximum finite generic degree D_k(n) of one directed coefficient over all acyclic mixed graphs whose directed part contains a supplied rooted spanning arborescence plus at most k extra arrows, including attaining families for every admissible (n,k).

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature's tractable boundary is k=0, where Mobius propagation leaves at most two finite coordinate values, while general graphical work studies rational uniqueness, infinite-to-one behavior, or full-parameter fibers. The adjacent CausalSmith run instead treats a supplied-covariance real singleton predicate and uses a growing number of two-parent sinks. Neither source controls the complex extension degree of one coordinate after exactly k added arrows, distinguishes coordinate projection from whole-fiber degree, or realizes the bound for every smaller n. The proposed orientation count can therefore fail through covariance-coefficient relations, saturation losses, or roots at infinity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit formula or structural recurrence for D_k(n), proved by a universal coordinate-degree upper bound and graph-query constructions attaining it on a nonempty Zariski-open set for every admissible (n,k).

method_exemplars.why_closest: Any recurrence must reduce to this coordinate-level k=0 mechanism and locate exactly how extra parents couple its one-dimensional components.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A multihomogeneous or mixed-volume count is generically sharp in an unrestricted coefficient space, whereas SEM covariance equations occupy a constrained coefficient subvariety; denominator saturation can also delete poles or components at infinity. Existing five-node SEM censuses test generic identifiability rather than exact extension degree of a queried coordinate in the rooted tree-plus-k class. Consequently a modular quartic or a raw Bezout count cannot validate the proposed all-n recurrence without characteristic-zero lifting and saturation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A machine-verifiable table of d_e for every rooted n<=5, k<=2 graph-query orbit, with saturated characteristic-zero elimination certificates and a theorem extracting corrected small-n base cases or a counterexample to the proposed recurrence.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available causal algorithms divide into a fast complete tree routine, general exponential-space-bounded decision machinery, and bounded-degree rational-formula search. Generic elimination and RUR machinery is not automatically fixed-parameter in the tree distance. The adjacent proposal deliberately avoids a global primitive element and treats poles and zero equations pointwise. The missing proof is a causal sparsity reduction showing that coordinate elimination, squarefreeness, pole exclusion, leading-coefficient stability, and lifting can all be encoded by rational arithmetic circuits of n^{O(k+1)} size; a discriminant alone does not exclude infinity components or zero-over-zero cancellation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Las Vegas or bounded-error algorithm with n^{C(k+1)} poly(log(1/delta)) construction time and certificate length that outputs d_e, a monic polynomial in K_G[t], and explicit nonvanishing covariance circuits whose complement guarantees that its roots equal the saturated generic coordinate projection.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing contrasts algebraic decidability with practically bounded symbolic output and is directly software-facing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Linear-SCM identification is algebraically decidable -> generic elimination is computationally prohibitive -> distance k from a tree should permit exact minimal-polynomial and exceptional-set certificates

method_exemplars.technique: Generic rational univariate representations with controlled specialization of parametric zero-dimensional systems.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A coordinate minimal polynomial and its valid-specialization locus are exactly the required univariate and exceptional-set objects.

method_exemplars.technique: Straight-line-program computation of multihomogeneous resultants with complexity controlled by support and resultant degree.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covariance equations have structured supports, while circuit-valued resultant coefficients match the requested output representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate recursively represented identifying equations and propagate covariance-estimation error through their computational graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Circuit coefficients and simple roots permit an analogous delta-method propagation for each regular branch.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Whole-fiber degree multiplication need not survive projection because distinct global branches can share one lambda_e value, while edge-wise determinant and ancestor methods stop at rational recovery. The missing object is a projection-aware rule involving the relevant subfield intersections, elimination ideals, or branch stabilizers; it must also remain valid when an extra parent couples pieces that previously decomposed. Without it, a recurrence in k can silently count joint branches rather than distinct queried-coordinate values.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving exact max, product, or lcm rules—or a finite structural recurrence—for coordinate extension degrees under mixed-component and ancestor decomposition, with counterexamples characterizing precisely when full-fiber factorization collapses after projection.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates identification at the individual-edge level and separates an edge query from recovery of the full parameter vector.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Whole-model criteria miss useful edge information -> determinantal relations isolate one coefficient -> projection-aware algebraic degree extends edge analysis beyond rational recovery

method_exemplars.technique: Tian-style mixed-component decomposition and algebraic degree multiplication for full generic fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed result must refine this full-fiber theorem to the image of a single coordinate.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Complex coordinate degree does not count real values, and a real coordinate root may fail to lift to a full real solution of the remaining structural equations. The adjacent proposal proves only that positive definiteness follows by congruence once a complete real supported coefficient matrix is already available. Existing RUR methods can isolate real solutions after obtaining a suitable zero-dimensional representation, but the new step is root-by-root saturated lifting data that preserves every missing-bidirected equation and distinguishes poles, infinity roots, and nonreal extensions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient semialgebraic lifting criterion and exact certificate algorithm that labels every simple real coordinate root as extendable or nonextendable to the supported real SCM fiber off an explicit discriminant-and-denominator exceptional set.

method_exemplars.technique: Separating linear forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact sign evaluation at all real solutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These operations can turn a coordinate polynomial plus lifting formulas into a certified enumeration of real pole-free structural branches.

method_exemplars.technique: Alpha-theory bounds and exact rational checks certifying isolated solutions of polynomial systems.

open_problems.why_unsolved: General set-inference theory does not exploit that this target is a finite collection of simple roots whose polynomial coefficients are smooth covariance functionals. Gaussian mixed-graph fitting typically targets identifiable models, while singularity theory shows why collisions and discriminant-zero points must be excluded. The adjacent fan-in run explicitly stops before approximate covariance and inference, and the snapshot proposal has only a population-centered local branch routine. The missing step is a uniform root-perturbation expansion coupled to covariance-model projection, exhaustive branch matching, and locally constant real-extension status.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sample-covariance/model-projection finite-set estimator with O_p(m^{-1/2}) Hausdorff error, a joint Gaussian limit and simultaneous valid neighborhoods for all locally labeled simple retained roots, and consistency plus asymptotic normality on singleton real fibers.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference for the entire observationally compatible set and organizes results around set consistency, rate, and coverage.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational restrictions can identify a set rather than a point -> sample analogues should estimate the full set -> finite algebraic SCM fibers require Hausdorff rates and simultaneous branch coverage

method_exemplars.technique: Criterion-level-set estimation, Hausdorff convergence, and confidence-region inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the general inferential architecture for the finite retained coordinate fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Tangent-cone analysis of semialgebraic likelihood models and diagnosis of nonstandard limits at singularities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It explains why the theorem must impose separated roots and avoid discriminant-zero strata.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate identification equations, propagate sample-moment error, and estimate a sandwich covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each simple branch is locally an implicit smooth covariance functional, so the same proof architecture yields its branchwise CLT.

literature_map:
1. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1003.1146) separate real positive-definite fibers, global injectivity, genericity, and explicit degree-two behavior.
2. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma (2010, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0812.1938) give trek-separation and determinant expansions underlying covariance equations.
3. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1107.5552) give half-trek criteria, mixed-component full-fiber degree factorization, and computations through five vertices, while leaving complete generic identification open.
4. Drton and Weihs (2016, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, arXiv:1504.02992) extend generic-identification tests through ancestor decomposition.
5. Weihs et al. (2018, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1702.03884) shift explicitly to single-edge queries but recover rational determinant formulas rather than higher coordinate degrees.
6. Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim (2019, NeurIPS, arXiv:1910.13493) provide polynomial-time graphical routes and hardness for a stronger determinantal search criterion.
7. van der Zander et al. (2022, AISTATS, arXiv:2203.01852) solve missing-cycle quadratic systems on tree-shaped directed parts.
8. Gupta and Blaser (2024, AAAI, arXiv:2311.14058) complete the tree case with degree 1, 2, or infinity and randomized PIT certificates.
9. Dorfler et al. (2024, arXiv:2407.12528) give a complete polynomial-space general identification algorithm and hardness evidence for supplied-covariance fiber questions.
10. Briefs and Blaser (2025, NeurIPS) accelerate the same tree-only predicate implemented by fasttreeid.
11. Adhikari, Gross, Harkonen, and Tsigaridas (2022, arXiv:2210.00239) study rational covariance parametrizations and generic finite-to-one behavior, but not the tree-plus-k coordinate frontier.
12. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma (2026, arXiv:2604.20516) search efficiently for bounded-degree rational formulas; algebraic minimal polynomials remain outside that deliverable.
13. Corniquel (2026, arXiv:2602.06817), Jeronimo and Sabia (2007), Emiris (1996), and Bouzidi et al. (2015) provide RUR, multihomogeneous-resultant, sparse-elimination, and real-root machinery not yet specialized to tree-plus-k covariance fibers.
14. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007), Drton (2009), Drton-Eichler-Richardson (2009), and Sturma-Drton-Leung (2024) cover set inference, singularities, mixed-graph fitting, and polynomial-constraint tests, but not simultaneous inference for regular finite coordinate fibers.
15. The unoccupied intersection is sharp single-coordinate complex degree in (n,k), with projection-aware reduction, fixed-parameter certificates, real-extension filtering, and regular finite-set inference.
prior_proposal_map:
The target run eid_extra_parent_degree/v1 contained only state metadata at scouting time, so it supplied no proposal core or reviewer evidence.
The highest-priority adjacent run was active/eid_fanin_numedge_frontier/v1; its proto_core, writeup, two angle reviews, and resolved few-two-parent artifacts were inspected.
That run contributed the generic tree 1/2/infinite base case, Mobius/2-CNF pointwise-fiber machinery, the componentwise primitive-element limitation, and explicit exclusions of stability and inference.
Its numerical K_G question was resolved through exact-fiber padding at indegree three and must not be recycled as the present generic tree-plus-k degree problem.
Reviewer angle0_v2 supplied the most relevant strengthening paths: an exceptional FASTP covariance and the growing two-parent count in the compiler.
The downgraded eid_snapshot_commonnoise_stabilizer/v1 core and bank note supplied an unresolved exhaustive branch-labeling problem and a local branchwise-inference template.
Banked finite-fiber count-data and DOG-completion proposals were inspected but were too remote to ground further Gaussian covariance-degree opportunities.
No relevant angle-rejected proposal occurred in the adjacent runs, and no mined prior run already stated the sharp single-coordinate D_k(n) frontier.
